title: Google Moved Roofing LSAs Into Google Ads: 6 Settings That Changed
html:
Quick answer: Google is moving roofing Local Services Ads (LSA) accounts into Google Ads as pay-per-lead Performance Max campaigns. Google named roofing in the first wave, which began in August 2026. Your ads still show in the same spots on Google Search and Maps, but six settings change: budgets, bidding, target CPA, performance history, BBB callouts, and profile syncing.

What Google Changed for Roofing LSAs

Google is retiring the standalone Local Services Ads dashboard. Every LSA account moves into Google Ads as a Performance Max campaign with pay-per-lead goals. Google has also said Performance Max may filter some brand traffic, so see brand searches in Performance Max before you migrate. Roofing sits in the first group Google named. Advertisers have also spotted new pay-per-lead terms inside Google Ads. Google is also testing AI Mode home services booking links through partner platforms.

The pay-per-lead model stays. You still pay only for valid calls and messages, not clicks. Your ads still show only on Google Search and Google Maps, in the same positions as before. Separately, Google is expanding ads in AI Mode for Search campaigns. The roofing Local Services Ads you know are not going away. The place you manage them is.

The rollout timeline

Phase Who moves When
Phase 1 Select U.S. home and storefront services, including roofing, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and pest control August 2026
Phase 2 Service-area businesses without a storefront, plus accounts with custom bidding or booking setups Late 2026
Phase 3 Non-U.S. accounts and all remaining categories 2027

Most roofing companies run as service-area businesses with no storefront. That means many roofers will land in Phase 2, not Phase 1. Check your inbox now either way. Google emails the account admin 14 days before migration, then sends a final reminder 7 days later. On migration day, the old LSA login redirects you to Google Ads.

The 6 Settings That Change on Migration Day

Six settings change the day your roofing LSA account moves. Google applies most of them automatically, so it's easy to miss what changed.

Setting Before (LSA dashboard) After (Google Ads)
Budget Weekly budget Daily average: weekly budget ÷ 7, monthly cap = daily × 30.4
Bidding Manual max cost per lead allowed Manual bidding removed
Target CPA Separate targets per service category One blended target per campaign
Performance history Impressions, spend, and reports in the dashboard Not carried over; past leads and call recordings do carry over
BBB badge BBB callout shown BBB callouts removed; add at least 6 structured callouts
Profile sync Edited inside LSA Name, address, hours sync one way from your Google Business Profile

1. Weekly budgets become daily budgets

Google divides your average weekly budget by 7. A $1,400 weekly budget becomes a $200 daily average. Daily spend can run higher on busy days, but the month caps at $200 × 30.4, or $6,080.

2. Your max cost-per-lead bid goes away

Google Ads does not support manual bidding on these campaigns. If you capped roofing leads at $90 each, that cap disappears. Google's automated bidding takes over.

3. Category targets merge into one

Many roofers run roofing, gutters, and siding in one LSA account with different target CPAs. After migration, Google calculates one campaign-level target for all of them. To keep separate targets, you need separate campaigns per service.

4. Your performance reports disappear

Past impressions, clicks, weekly spend, and ad reports do not move to Google Ads. Your lead history does. Google says a download page is coming, and it tells advertisers to screenshot reports now if they need them.

5. The BBB callout is gone

Google no longer supports BBB callouts. It asks advertisers to pick at least 6 other structured callouts, such as specialties, hours, or payment methods.

6. Your Google Business Profile now drives your ads

Business name, address, and hours sync from your Google Business Profile into Google Ads. A big change to your name, address, or primary category triggers a 24 to 48 hour review. Your campaign may pause during that review.

What This Means for Roofing Companies

Roofing feels this change more than most trades because roofing leads cost more. Ignite Visibility estimates roofing LSA leads at $60 to $150 each, the top of the home services range it lists. When each lead costs that much, losing bid control or pausing for two days costs real money.

Storm season pauses. A roofing company that changes its address or primary category in Google Business Profile during hail season can trigger a 24 to 48 hour review. That pause can cost a week of storm calls in a single weekend. Make profile changes before storm season, not during it. Blended cost per lead. Roof replacement leads justify a higher bid than gutter cleaning leads. One blended target can push spend toward cheaper, lower-value jobs. Split campaigns by service if your margins differ by job type. No baseline to judge results. Google warns performance can take up to two weeks to stabilize. Without your old reports, you can't tell if a dip is the migration or the market. Export your numbers before the switch. Anna Anderson of A-Squared Marketing told Roofing Contractor that small mismatches across Google accounts can have a big impact. Her advice: clean up your business name, address, phone, ownership, and license details before your migration email arrives. There is good news too. Your Google Verified status and badge carry over automatically. Google also says insurance and license reverification are no longer required at migration.

Before Your Migration Email Arrives

The 14-day notice gives you two weeks, and you cannot pause the switch. Run these checks on every roofing LSA account now, before Google picks the date. Before you sign with a local agency, compare Orlando pest control lead generation agencies.

The First Two Weeks After Migration

Google says to allow up to two weeks for a migrated campaign to settle. Hold off on big changes during that window, but watch these numbers daily.

After day 14, split campaigns by service if your lead mix drifted. You can't build new pay-per-lead campaigns inside Google Ads yet, so Google points advertisers to g.co/localservices for that step.

Are Google Local Services Ads going away for roofers?

No. Google is moving Local Services Ads into Google Ads, not ending them. Roofing companies still pay per valid lead, and ads still show at the top of Google Search and Maps. What changes is where you manage budgets, bids, and leads. The old LSA dashboard closes once your account migrates.
